definition: the five different systems that can make a thing automatic in me

settled:
They are sensory habituation, picking things up socially without trying, a response fired by an outside cue, fitting new things into what I already know, and running a sequence of actions as one.

Three are reduced in me and two are intact. Nothing sensory gets quieter with exposure, so that load is permanent. Social rules never came in by watching, so I studied them and fitted them in by the fourth route instead. And a sequence I start myself stays explicit forever: after thousands of goes, brushing my teeth still runs off a list I am reading.

The third one is intact in me and the fifth one is not, so the third carries the fifth's work on top of its own.

It does that at three widths of cue: a word, a circumstance in a room, and the state of the system in front of me. The shape is the same at all three.

Going into it deliberately rather than picking it up starts slower than the usual route and finishes higher.

title: The Five Ways Something Becomes Automatic
